learningObjective: See how per-arm sample size and metric variance jointly determine the minimum effect an experiment can reliably detect.
mediumRationale: A deterministic SVG is the smallest medium that makes the inverse-square-root sample-size relationship and the linear variance relationship spatial and quantitatively checkable. Mermaid expresses topology rather than numerical curves; semantic HTML could list values but would hide their shape; interaction adds controls without improving this fixed comparison; paper-figure reuse is unnecessary and permission for source figures was not established; mixed media adds no teaching value; and no visual leaves the article's hardest quantitative intuition in formula form only.

pages.insight: The search-system example separates offline ranking metrics from online A/B-test outcomes such as search engagement and days with a play.

The system-design walkthrough makes experimentation the final step, asks for a specific effect hypothesis such as a 0.5% engagement lift, and asks how much offline data is needed before online evaluation.
The production-serving checklist calls for model-gating experiments, constraint checks, monitored metrics, and user feedback.
The Rules of Machine Learning Engineering slide says to measure model deltas, quantify undesirable behavior, and not equate identical short-term behavior with identical long-term behavior.

deckReview.notes: The complete 214-page Basic_ML_CS_concepts deck was searched by extracted text for A/B testing, experimentation, online metrics, statistical power, sample size, hypotheses, novelty, and spillovers. Pages 141, 164, 168, and 169 and their neighboring pages were then read directly. They establish the offline-to-online decision context but contain no power or minimum-detectable-effect plot, so no deck figure is reused.

sources.title: Controlled experiments on the web: survey and practical guide
sources.usage: Used as the primary reference for randomized online experiments, practical validity checks, power, and decision framing.
sources.license: The publisher page does not grant figure-reuse rights for this site. No figure, table, wording, or empirical values were copied; the source is cited for concepts only.

sources.title: Improving the Sensitivity of Online Controlled Experiments by Utilizing Pre-Experiment Data
sources.usage: Used to verify that reducing metric variance improves experiment sensitivity and therefore lowers the detectable effect at fixed sample size.
sources.license: ACM publication does not imply permission to republish its figures. No figure, data, or prose was copied; CUPED is referenced conceptually only.

sources.title: statsmodels TTestIndPower.solve_power documentation
sources.usage: Used as official statistical-software documentation to cross-check two-independent-sample power inputs, equal allocation, two-sided testing, effect-size definition, alpha, and power.
sources.license: No documentation figure or wording was copied. The plotted values are an original calculation from the stated normal approximation.

sourceReview.notes: The SVG is an original mathematical construction, not a redraw of a source figure. It uses the stated equal-arm normal approximation with two-sided alpha 0.05, 80% power, z values 1.96 and 0.84, and illustrative metric standard deviations of 1 and 2 units. At N = 1,000, 4,000, and 16,000 per arm, the rounded MDE values are 0.125, 0.063, and 0.031 metric units for sigma = 1, and exactly twice those values for sigma = 2.

agentReview.summary: Reviewed the complete article, full-deck text search and relevant slide neighborhoods, the primary online-experiment literature, and official two-sample power documentation. The hardest mental model is how sample size and noise jointly set sensitivity, so the review selected one compact, original MDE curve comparison.

implementation.accessibility: The SVG has a title and a complete description containing its assumptions and all six plotted values. The two series differ by solid versus dashed line style and are directly labeled, while axis labels, point markers, value callouts, and the text caption preserve the lesson without color. A compact 360-unit viewBox uses the existing responsive, theme-aware, and print-aware figure primitives.
